content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: Critics of the Green New Deal argue that the ambitious climate plan will stifle job creation and harm the economy, despite its supporters claiming it will create millions of green jobs.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: Economists from conservative think tanks warn that the proposed massive government intervention in the energy sector could lead to higher costs and fewer employment opportunities in traditional industries.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: Proponents counter that the Green New Deal will actually boost the economy through investments in renewable energy and infrastructure, which they say will outpace any potential losses.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: The debate over the Green New Deal highlights the ongoing tension between environmental sustainability and economic growth, a central issue in American politics.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_4
content_blocks.text: One expert noted, 'We can't afford to ignore the economic consequences of such drastic policy changes.'

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: 'The Green New Deal is a dangerous distraction from real economic challenges,' said John Doe, a leading economist at the Center for Economic Research.
